quality.title: Optimisation quality (healthy network)
quality.question: With working communications and a working coordinator, how well does each strategy dispatch?

normal.description: Steady river rise, honest reports. Demonstrates routine negotiation and shelter reservations.

flash_flood.description: Water rises three times faster; low-lying roads close early and boats carry most rescues.

resource_shortage.description: Only 3 boats and 2 ground teams are available for the same demand.

shelter_overflow.description: Riverside Civic Arena loses most of its capacity at t=25 (power failure).

contradictory.description: Noisy, duplicated, delayed and contradictory SOS reports, including false alarms and a 3-tick comms delay.

resilience.title: Failure resilience
resilience.question: Under infrastructure, coordinator and network failures: how much service is lost, how fast is it recovered, and does safety hold?

triple_failure.description: At t=22 a bridge in use closes, a committed boat fails and a shelter with inbound arrivals overflows — simultaneously.

bridge_closure.description: Central Bridge is closed by structural damage at t=15 while units depend on it.

coordinator_outage.description: Central dispatch fails at t=15 for 60 minutes. Existing missions continue; peer communication and local safety remain available. No standby coordinator is modelled.

network_partition.description: At t=20 three boats and Riverside Civic Arena are split from the rest of the network for 40 minutes. Committed missions continue; no new commitments cross the split.

lossy_network.description: Agent messages take 1 minute per hop and 15% are lost or duplicated. Affects the message-passing strategy; agents recover through timeouts and idempotent handling.

report_noise.title: Service vs SOS report noise
report_noise.question: How does dispatch quality degrade as reports become noisier (wrong counts, urgency, location)?

message_loss.title: Service vs message loss (message-passing agents, 1 min/hop)
message_loss.question: How much service does the message-passing protocol lose as the radio network drops more messages?
